newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ashdown tells fellow leaders calm down.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ashdown tells fellow leaders calm down.

text.p: Britain's Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown on Tuesday urged his political partners to calm down and lessen the hectic pace of their campaigning in the leadup to the May 1 election.
"My advice to both of them is to calm down," Ashdown told Prime Minister John Major and opposition Labour leader Tony Blair at the start of Britain's longest election campaign in 80 years,
"We have got six weeks to go. If we go on at this pace, people are going to be fed up to the back teeth with the whole thing," he told GMTV.
He also said: "Get off the insults, get off the posters ... I am just fed up to the back teeth and I think most people are too with this campaign of posters and insults."
"I want to break this destructive 'Ya-boo' politics that we see so much of," he said.
The centrist leader repeated his party's specific pledges on higher direct taxes to pay for better education.
"The total package that we are asking people to pay is 45 pence a week. That's a packet of peanuts in the pub, half a lottery ticket."
Ashdown said he planned to interrupt his campaigning for the birth of his daughter's child. She is married to a Frenchman and lives in France.
"If I become a grandfather during the middle of this campaign you won't see me for dust." he said.
